angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 499,513 km at 109.11 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.1653 +/- 0.0172 mas (same row, RUWE 0.76): 109.11 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.718 +/- 0.008 solar radii from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-36 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract): 499,513 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.79 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-36 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4916 +/- 37 K from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-36 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-36 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-36.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.623, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
